howDoI.q: How do I choose how many hit points my hero starts with?
How do I make a block that takes hit points?
How do I make a pickup that gives hit points back?
Do hit points carry from one level to the next?
How do I make my hero lose a life when his hit points run out?
Can a heart give my hero more than he started with?
How do I give my hero an extra life?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Health and Hearts is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels about hit points, hearts and lives, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: Hit Points
pages.html:
Level 1: Hit Points

The F2 SHOWS YOUR HIT POINTS sign comes first: press F2 and Kit’s numbers appear. He starts with 30 hit points and 3 lives. The A SPIKE TAKES 10 HIT POINTS sign stands before a single spike. Walk into it and it stings: Kit shows his hurt pose and has 20 left. The spike then lies flat and harmless. Press F2 again to see.

Four coins are worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Hit points to start. Open hero.chr in the character editor. The first counter, Hit points, is 30, and Lives is 3. Each time a life is lost, the room starts again with the hit points back at that number.
  • A block that takes them. Open hearts.bbl in the blocks editor and pick spikeUp. Its Hit points is −10. The engine adds that to the hero each tick the block overlaps him, so a block that only hurts would drain him in a second.
  • Once. The same block has Becomes block set to spikeFlat, which has no hit points. One touch, one sting, the way a coin vanishes when you take it.
  • You see it. The hero’s Hurt sequence plays, with its sound, each time his hit points drop. The count itself is on F2, the game’s own status screen.
  • Where it is. Open one.map in the map editor. The spike is one block on the grass, painted like grass.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with words drawn in their pictures.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door to the next level. Open hearts.gam in the scenes editor.

pages.head: Level 2: Hearts Heal
pages.html:
Level 2: Hearts Heal

Kit arrives with the 20 hit points he left level 1 with. The A HEART GIVES 10 HIT POINTS BACK sign comes first. Another spike takes him down to 10, and then two hearts in a row bring him up to 30. Each heart is gone once he touches it. The HIT POINTS GO WITH YOU TO THE NEXT ROOM sign is by the exit, because they do.

Three coins are on the way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A pickup that heals. In hearts.bbl pick heart. Its Hit points is +10: the same field as the spike, above zero instead of below. The engine plays a soft sound for it.
  • Gone when touched. Becomes block is set to the sky block, so the heart disappears and gives its 10 only once.
  • No stop at 30. Nothing in the engine keeps hit points at the number a hero started with. Level 3 uses that.
  • They carry on. Hit points are kept as the hero goes through a door. They only go back to the starting number when a life is lost or a new game starts.
  • Where they are. Open two.map. The spike and the two hearts stand on the grass, painted like anything else.

pages.head: Level 3: Lives
pages.html:
Level 3: Lives

Four spikes stand along the ground, spaced out so each stings on its own. That is 40, and Kit has 30. The AT ZERO HIT POINTS YOU LOSE A LIFE sign says what happens: walk straight along the ground and the third spike takes his last hit point. He falls over, a life is gone (press F2) and the room starts again, with 30 hit points.

This time jump up onto the ledge first. Two hearts sit on it, and the HEARTS CAN TAKE YOU PAST 30 sign says why that is fine: 50 hit points get him past all four spikes. Near the end a ledge holds a smiling face in a teal beanie. The A FACE ADDS A LIFE sign says the rest.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • Zero costs a life. No block takes a life here. When the hero’s hit points reach zero the engine plays his Die sequence, takes one life and starts the same level again. With no lives left, the game ends.
  • Where he comes back. At the place he arrived the first time: the cyan marker on the doorway of three.map. Drag it to change that.
  • What starts over. The map is read again, so hearts, spikes and coins are all back. Your score stays.
  • Past where he started. Two heart blocks on a ledge of planks bring 30 to 50. The planks are solid on top only, so Kit jumps up through them and stands on top.
  • An extra life. Pick oneUp in hearts.bbl. Its Effect is counter 1 (lives) and the Amount is 1. It is gone when touched.
  • Spaced spikes. Spikes in a row can share one sting while Kit is in his hurt pose. Three blocks apart, each one counts.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Give Kit 50 hit points in hero.chr and see how level 3 changes.
  • Make heart give 30 instead of 10.
  • Make spikeUp take 15, and count how many Kit can walk through.
  • Give Kit 1 life in hero.chr, and lose it in level 3.
  • Move a oneUp face somewhere harder to reach.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
